diagnosis: All 4 rollouts revealed all four facts (PF1–PF4) via reveal actions and cited them in justification_fact_ids, so there are no disclosure or telepathy problems. The gate failed because checks C2, C4, C5, C6, and C7 failed in every single rollout (0/4 each) despite the underlying information being present in the settlements — a systematic ENCODING MISMATCH. C1 and C3 pass 4/4 because they check the primary decision fields (affected_record_count=2736, massachusetts_ag_filing_required=true) that the model naturally produces. C2 (PF1) likely expects a dedicated field for the exposed data elements (names, email addresses, unencrypted SSNs) that the model only embeds in commitment detail text, not in a structured decision field. C4 (PF2) likely expects a separate field capturing the same-day filing timing, but the model only outputs the boolean massachusetts_ag_filing_required. C5, C6, and C7 fail even though the decisions contain consumer_remedy, insurer_consent_required_before_remediation, and no_admission_language_required with correct values, meaning the checks' expected field names or value formats do not match the model's natural encoding.

C5.why: The draft has no fixed customer remedy or liability wording; PF4 changes both to 24 months of identity restoration and an express no-admission-of-negligence statement.

C7.why: The draft has no fixed customer remedy or liability wording; PF4 changes both to 24 months of identity restoration and an express no-admission-of-negligence statement.

C6.why: Without the policy endorsement, the package could promise identity restoration without an insurer condition; PF3 changes it to require written consent before that remediation is promised or provided.

C4.why: The ordinary draft does not require a Massachusetts Attorney General filing sequence; PF2 changes the package to require that filing no later than the same day as consumer notices.

C2.why: The draft leaves the count undetermined and does not identify the exposed data elements; PF1 changes the filing to exactly 2,736 accounts and names the specific combination of exposed information.
